s1.syndrome_frame: Asymptomatic hepatic masses with abnormal liver function tests
salient_findings: Mildly elevated liver enzymes (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT)
key_facts: 48-year-old man with no prior medical history
Three hepatic masses in segments 1, 6, and 2
Mass sizes: 67×53 mm, 13 mm, and 9 mm
Normal total bilirubin (0.6 mg/dL) and albumin (4.2 g/dL)
Mildly elevated AST (37 IU/L) and ALT (70 IU/L)
Mildly elevated ALP (176 U/L) and GGT (170 IU/L)
Normal alpha-fetoprotein (2.9 ng/mL), PIVKA-II (11 mAU/mL), and CA19-9 (4.0 IU/L)
Dynamic contrast-enhanced CT showed peripheral early ring enhancement and heterogeneous internal enhancement
EOB-MRI showed hypointense mass on T1-weighted images and hyperintense areas on T2-weighted images
FDG-PET showed no radiotracer accumulation in any of the hepatic lesions
Hepatic arteriography demonstrated hypervascular masses without pooling

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple hepatic masses with peripheral early ring enhancement and heterogeneous internal enhancement on CT, consistent with hepatocellular adenoma

shortlist.label: Focal nodular hyperplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Hypointense mass on T1-weighted images and hyperintense areas on T2-weighted images on MRI, consistent with focal nodular hyperplasia

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypervascular masses on hepatic arteriography without pooling, consistent with hemangioma

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mildly elevated ALP and GGT, and abnormal liver function tests, raising concern for intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma

shortlist.label: Hepatic metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple hepatic masses, although tumor markers are within normal limits, metastasis cannot be entirely ruled out

raw.rationale: The patient's imaging findings, including peripheral early ring enhancement on dynamic contrast-enhanced CT and hypointense mass on T1-weighted images with hyperintense areas on T2-weighted images on EOB-MRI, are characteristic of hemangioma. Additionally, the lack of radiotracer accumulation on FDG-PET and the presence of hypervascular masses without pooling on hepatic arteriography support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular adenoma
rejected.why: Normal alpha-fetoprotein levels and lack of significant liver function abnormalities make this less likely

rejected.label: Focal nodular hyperplasia
rejected.why: Typically shows central scar on imaging, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: Would likely cause more significant liver function abnormalities and elevated tumor markers

rejected.label: Hepatic metastasis
rejected.why: No primary malignancy mentioned and tumor markers are within normal limits
